title: Status Page v2 — Component Mapping (Working Notes)
body:
Context / why this doc exists
- Current public status page components are too coarse, leading to mismatches (e.g., “API Operational” while Embeddings failing; Streaming disconnects not represented).
- Goal: propose a v2 component list and the mapping rules from internal signals/services → public components, with attention to edge cases (partial region impact, latency-only degradation, etc.).
- This is intentionally messy working notes. Canonical list will eventually live in the component registry (see ADR discussions in #architecture).

Non-goals (for now)
- Not defining new internal SLOs here (we’ll align later).
- Not solving Dedicated/Private customer-specific visibility (we need guidance from Kira + Legal).
- Not finalizing exact Statuspage UI grouping (Design is doing layout separately).

Guiding principles (rough)
1) Components should match how customers think about the product: “Chat/Completions”, “Streaming”, “Embeddings”, etc.
2) Split by region when customer impact is region-scoped and actionable.
3) Avoid components that require exposing sensitive capacity info (esp. Dedicated/Private).
4) If we cannot reliably detect impact at a component level, don’t create the component yet (or mark it “manual only” while instrumentation catches up).
5) Favor a small number of stable components over hyper-granular components that flap.

Proposed component model (v2)
We’re aiming for a matrix: product_surface x region x capability. Some capabilities are global-only.

Regions (initial proposal)
- us-east
- us-west
- eu-west
- ap-southeast
- global (used only when region attribution is impossible or impact is truly cross-region)

Capabilities / product surfaces (customer-facing)
Hosted API (token generation)
- Chat/Completions API
- Streaming (SSE/websocket streaming delivery)
- Tool/function calling (tentative: may be folded into Chat/Completions unless we have clear separate failure modes)

Hosted API (non-generation)
- Embeddings
- Reranking

Platform / Control surfaces
- Console
- Authentication & API Keys (auth/token issuance, key validation)
- Webhooks/Callbacks (if applicable; TBD whether we expose publicly)

Dedicated
- Dedicated Control Plane (provisioning, scaling actions, deploy/rollout operations)
- Dedicated Data Plane (request serving) — open question: do we represent this publicly as a component at all, or only as a generic “Dedicated” status?

Private
- Private Control Plane — likely NOT public (customer/network-specific). We need a policy path.

Proposed component list (for public Statuspage)
Note: names are “customer labels”; ids will be snake_case or kebab-case in registry.

A) Hosted API — per region
- Hosted API: Chat/Completions (us-east)
- Hosted API: Chat/Completions (us-west)
- Hosted API: Chat/Completions (eu-west)
- Hosted API: Chat/Completions (ap-southeast)

- Hosted API: Streaming (us-east)
- Hosted API: Streaming (us-west)
- Hosted API: Streaming (eu-west)
- Hosted API: Streaming (ap-southeast)

- Hosted API: Embeddings (us-east)
- Hosted API: Embeddings (us-west)
- Hosted API: Embeddings (eu-west)
- Hosted API: Embeddings (ap-southeast)

- Hosted API: Reranking (us-east)
- Hosted API: Reranking (us-west)
- Hosted API: Reranking (eu-west)
- Hosted API: Reranking (ap-southeast)

B) Platform — global
- Redwood Console (global)
- Authentication & API Keys (global)

C) Dedicated — global (initial)
- Redwood Dedicated: Control Plane (global)
- Redwood Dedicated: Data Plane (global) (TBD; may be too broad / not always accurate)

Why Dedicated is global-only for now:
- Customers may have capacity in specific regions, but public page shouldn’t reveal per-customer deployments.
- We can still mention “Dedicated customers may be impacted” in incident text with careful wording.

Mapping rules (high-level)
Definition: component is a public label; mapping is how we decide which component(s) to mark based on internal evidence.

Rule 0: Only mark a component as impacted if we can support it with metrics OR confirmed reports.
- Metrics path: alert thresholds / dashboards.
- Reports path: multiple independent signals (support tickets + internal repro + logs). If reports-only, use “Investigating” and update frequently.

Rule 1: Prefer smallest correct scope
- If streaming-only is failing, don’t mark Chat/Completions.
- If embeddings-only is failing, don’t mark “Hosted API: Chat/Completions”.

Rule 2: Region attribution
- Use request region inferred from gateway metrics (component tags) when possible.
- If we only see global error spikes but can’t attribute (e.g., shared dependency), mark “global” only if it affects multiple regions.
- If we suspect single region but are not sure, either:
  a) Mark suspected region and caveat in text (“we are investigating elevated errors in us-east”), OR
  b) Mark all regions only if evidence suggests broad impact (avoid premature blast radius inflation).

Rule 3: Capability detection
- Streaming: use streaming disconnect/error counters and time-to-first-token (TTFT) anomalies specific to streaming endpoints.
- Chat/Completions: use non-streaming request error rates + p95/p99 latency.
- Embeddings/Reranking: use endpoint-specific metrics.

Rule 4: Latency-only degradations
- We should allow “Degraded Performance” for latency-only, but thresholds must be conservative to avoid flapping.
- Open question: if p99 latency degrades while errors remain low, does that warrant public status? Current leaning: yes if sustained + user-visible (e.g., >X minutes and >Y% of requests exceed Z seconds).

Rule 5: Anti-flap / hysteresis
- Require sustained breach to flip to Degraded (e.g., 10-15 min window) and sustained recovery to flip back (e.g., 20-30 min).
- If it oscillates, keep component degraded and update incident text; don’t flip repeatedly.

Rule 6: Incident text should include capability + region + symptom, but avoid sensitive details
- OK: “elevated 5xx responses”, “increased latency”, “streaming disconnects”, “intermittent timeouts”.
- Avoid: “GPU capacity exhausted for customer X”, “provider outage in AZ Y”, exact customer traffic patterns.

Internal signal candidates by component (draft)
Hosted API: Chat/Completions (region)
- gateway.http_5xx_rate{route_group=chat_completions, region}
- gateway.request_latency_p99{route_group=chat_completions, region}
- scheduler.queue_time_p95{region} (only if strong correlation; careful about false positives)

Hosted API: Streaming (region)
- gateway.streaming_disconnect_rate{region}
- gateway.streaming_error_rate{region}
- streaming.ttft_p95{region} (if available)

Hosted API: Embeddings (region)
- gateway.http_5xx_rate{route_group=embeddings, region}
- gateway.request_latency_p99{route_group=embeddings, region}

Hosted API: Reranking (region)
- gateway.http_5xx_rate{route_group=rerank, region}
- gateway.request_latency_p99{route_group=rerank, region}

Console (global)
- console.web_5xx_rate
- console.page_load_p95 (maybe too noisy)
- login failures (ties into Auth)

Authentication & API Keys (global)
- auth.key_validation_error_rate
- token issuance failures
- elevated 401/403 at gateway with known-good keys (danger: false positives if customer misconfig)

Dedicated Control Plane (global)
- deploy/rollout job failure rate
- provisioning API error rate
- control plane latency

Dedicated Data Plane (global)
- hard: we don’t have a single global metric without mixing customers.
- possible approach: only show “Dedicated Data Plane” as impacted if multiple dedicated tenants show correlated error spikes AND it’s a platform-wide issue.
- may be manual-only at first.

Service-to-component mapping (draft)
We need to map internal service names and route groups into customer-facing components.

Route group → component capability
- /v1/chat/completions → Hosted API: Chat/Completions
- /v1/completions (legacy) → Hosted API: Chat/Completions (or separate? vote: fold in)
- /v1/embeddings → Hosted API: Embeddings
- /v1/rerank → Hosted API: Reranking
- streaming=true + /v1/chat/completions → Hosted API: Streaming

Internal service signals → component hints
- api-gateway: source of truth for request-level errors/latency, best for capability + region attribution.
- runtime-scheduler / batching: can indicate widespread latency, but should not directly toggle public status without gateway corroboration.
- model-registry / rollouts: can explain “increased errors due to a rollout”; impact still mapped through gateway.

Edge cases / scenarios
1) Partial region impact (single AZ, subset of pods)
- Metrics may show modest error rate increase, but customers see intermittent failures.
- Proposed handling:
  - If error rate crosses threshold: mark that region component degraded.
  - If below threshold but credible reports: consider degraded with “intermittent” language OR open incident without changing component state (needs policy).
- Open question: should we allow an “Informational” incident without component degradation when impact is real but too narrow to trip thresholds?

2) Streaming impacted, non-streaming fine
- Historically: status page only had “API” and was misleading.
- v2: mark Hosted API: Streaming (region). Keep Chat/Completions operational unless we see errors there too.
- Comms template should explicitly say “non-streaming requests are not impacted” when true.

3) Embeddings failing but chat fine
- v2: mark Hosted API: Embeddings (region).
- Need to validate our classification logic; there was at least one misclassification bug previously.

4) Latency spikes during throttling / rate limiting changes
- If customers are being rate limited due to their own quota, this should not be a public incident.
- Need a classifier: platform-induced elevated 429 across many tenants vs normal per-tenant quota enforcement.
- Open question: should we have a component for “Rate limiting/Quotas”? Leaning no; treat as incident text detail if it’s a platform regression.

5) Model-specific regressions (one model version)
- If a single model is broken, should we reflect that in components?
- Likely not via components (too granular); use incident text and mention affected model(s) where safe.
- Alternative: include “Model: <name>” field internally and show in post-incident summary only.

6) Console showing stale status vs actual status
- Should be a Console incident if Console cannot display incident details (UX integration).
- But avoid dual incidents unless truly separate.

7) Dependency outages (cloud provider, DNS, KMS)
- If it impacts Hosted API across multiple regions, we may need to mark multiple region components at once.
- Don’t attribute to vendor publicly unless approved; use “upstream dependency” language.

8) Dedicated/Private incidents
- Need rules:
  - If a Dedicated tenant is impacted due to customer config: no public incident.
  - If Dedicated control plane is down for all: public component + incident.
  - If a platform-wide data-plane regression affects many Dedicated tenants: maybe public component.
  - Private: almost always not public; may require direct customer comms.

Open questions (need decisions)
- Q1: Do we expose “Hosted API: Tool Calling” as a component?
  - Pros: function calling failures are real and distinct.
  - Cons: hard to reliably detect without parsing payload/tool_call errors; likely maps to Chat/Completions anyway.
  - Current leaning: no separate component in v1 rollout; revisit after instrumentation.

- Q2: Do we include a “Global API” component?
  - I think no; region-specific is more actionable. Global only for truly global things like Auth/Console.

- Q3: What’s the policy for low-severity, partial impact that doesn’t exceed thresholds?
  - Options: (a) incident without component degradation, (b) component degraded with “intermittent” language, (c) no public incident.
  - Need input from Support + SRE (customer expectation vs noise).

- Q4: When do we mark multiple regions vs one?
  - Proposed: require evidence per region (metrics or reports). But if the root cause is clearly global (e.g., auth outage), mark global component.

- Q5: Dedicated data plane component: publish or not?
  - Risk: ambiguous, might cause confusion for Hosted-only customers.
  - If we do publish, it should be clearly labeled “Dedicated (Reserved Capacity)”.

- Q6: How do we handle “degraded performance” thresholds across capabilities?
  - For streaming, user pain is often disconnects, not just latency.
  - For embeddings, latency thresholds might be different due to payload sizes.

Concrete next steps / action items
- Christine: turn this into a proposed registry structure + initial component ids (by 11/24).
- Mina: confirm region taxonomy and naming (us-east vs us-east-1) and what we can reliably infer from gateway tags (by 11/25).
- Allison + Aisha: propose initial thresholds and anti-flap windows per component (by 11/27).
- Ravi + Logan: validate route_group tagging coverage in gateway metrics; list gaps (by 11/27).
- Devon: confirm incident-bot intake fields can support this matrix (component + region + capability) (in progress).

Notes from recent incident threads (memory dump)
- During the us-east streaming degradation, we debated marking “API” vs “Streaming”. Outcome: we need a streaming-specific component and region-specific panels.
- Support feedback: customers are OK with “investigating” updates that admit uncertainty, but not OK with a green status page during real impact.
- Anti-flap: folks hate toggling; better to keep a component degraded for longer and explain progress than to flap.

Appendix: candidate component id patterns
- hosted-api.chat.us-east
- hosted-api.streaming.us-east
- hosted-api.embeddings.eu-west
- platform.console.global
- platform.auth.global
- dedicated.control-plane.global

Appendix: draft incident titles (for consistency)
- “Elevated errors for Hosted API: Embeddings (us-east)”
- “Degraded streaming connectivity for Hosted API: Streaming (eu-west)”
- “Authentication failures affecting API requests (global)”

End (for now) — please add comments inline rather than rewriting the whole doc; we’ll collapse into the registry spec once decisions land.
